gaps.sentence: He left ___ school at sixteen and went straight into a job.
gaps.explanation: Leave school (finish education) takes no article.

gaps.sentence: ___ disabled are offered free entry on Sundays.
gaps.explanation: 'The disabled' = disabled people as a group.

gaps.sentence: It was such ___ awful weather that we stayed indoors.
gaps.explanation: Uncountable nouns take no article after 'such': such awful weather.

gaps.sentence: It's ___ one-way street, so you can't turn left here.
gaps.explanation: 'One' starts with /w/, a consonant sound, so 'a one-way street'.

gaps.sentence: ___ most people agree that change is needed.
gaps.explanation: 'Most people' in a general sense takes no article.

gaps.sentence: She earns her living as ___ journalist.
gaps.explanation: Jobs after 'as' take a/an: as a journalist.
'The capital of Italy' — the of-phrase makes it unique and definite.

gaps.sentence: She gets up at six and watches ___ morning news.
gaps.explanation: 'The morning news' — a specific known broadcast, so 'the'.
